events.content: Audited the live model-pin state against ADR-080 rule 1 for issue #2840
Traced why scripts/validation/check_model_pins.py reported zero violations on those three files
Exposed the already-computed typed structure instead of adding a second parser
Taught check_model_pins.py to see a pin nested below the top level and to reject it outright
Removed the three nested versioned pins and regenerated the customer-facing mirrors
Ran two negative controls with teeth
Ran two negative controls with teeth      Blinding the gate to nested pins fails 3 of the 6 new tests; dropping the parser's typed field fails 4. Restoring both returns 27 passed.
Close the three bypasses an adversarial review found in the nested-pin check

lessons: When a governance gate reports clean against a violation you can see, suspect the parser before the policy. Dump what the parser actually returns for the offending file. Here it returned metadata as an empty string, which located the hole in one step.

Avoid: Hand-rolling a second frontmatter parse to reach data the shared parser already computed. Expose the typed structure the shared parser already builds for validation, and read it from the caller.

A cycle guard and a cost guard are different problems. The recursion-path form terminates on cycles and still permits exponential re-walking of a DAG, so 'it no longer crashes' is not evidence that the walk is bounded.
